title: Adaptive memory-bandwidth-aware kernel hinting for MIG overlap and prefill pipelining
creator: Maya Kapoor
description:
Goal: reduce p99 prefill latency and stabilize decode throughput when multiple MIG partitions share the same physical GPU by selecting kernels based on real-time memory-bandwidth signals and lightweight probe batches. Background: current kernel selection uses static heuristics tuned for whole-GPU profiles and often mis-predicts when many small MIG partitions or mixed vacillation of NVLink traffic are present. This causes prefills to either choose memory-heavy kernels that saturate shared DRAM bandwidth (spiking latency) or conservative kernels that waste compute headroom (reducing throughput).

Proposed approach: implement a memory-bandwidth-aware hinting layer that augments the kernel selector with three runtime signals: (1) per-MIG moving-average of memory bandwidth utilization (sampled from nvidia-smi / NVML counters), (2) short probe micro-batches to estimate effective kernel memory footprint and latency on the current partition mix, and (3) KV cache hit/miss pressure. The selector will prefer narrower-memory kernels (reduced workspace) when bandwidth > threshold_T_high, and prefer compute-dense kernels when bandwidth < threshold_T_low. Additionally, when two or more partitions show high contention we will enable prefill pipelining: interleaving small decode micro-batches across partitions to hide tail latency.

Constraints and safety: changes must not increase steady-state token cost materially, must respect per-request SLOs, and must fail open (revert to baseline kernel choices) on telemetry anomalies. We will limit automated clock/clock-boost suggestions to read-only telemetry initially; any active clock steering requires a follow-up RFC and infra guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: p99 prefill latency reduced by >=10% on target mixed-MIG testbed (H100 small partitions + L40S medium partitions) under synthetic 80% bandwidth load
no more than 3% regression in aggregate throughput (tokens/sec) across representative RLHF-like workloads
feature can be toggled per-node and per-customer (console flag and API config)
comprehensive unit and integration tests covering probe micro-batch timeouts and NVML counter fallbacks
production rollout gated by canary with traffic-splitting and automatic rollback on SLO breach
comments: 2025-03-13 - initial spike: ran baseline tests on h100-mig-1g/2g mix. Observed 22% p99 prefill regressions when partition churn is high. - Maya

2025-03-15 - design review notes from runtime team: prefer probe micro-batches no larger than 4 tokens or 2 micro-batches per second to keep overhead <0.5%. Avoid central counters; use per-node estimators. - Review by Aaron Wu
2025-03-16 - telemetry experiment: implemented bandwidth sampler using NVML EV counters (DRAM_Read/Write). Preliminary signals correlate with p99 (pearson=0.71). - Ethan

2025-03-18 - perf run: hinting enabled with conservative thresholds. Results: p99 prefill down 12% on mixed testbed; aggregate throughput up 4% for long-context streams, but 1.8% throughput regression on short-context micro-batched jobs. We'll add a context-length heuristic to avoid regressions. - Ethan

2025-03-19 - safety review: feature defaults to OFF for dedicated customers until runtime-1.20 rollout is approved. Added separate console toggle and per-customer opt-in. - Security/Compliance asked for audit log events when hinting toggles applied. - Maya
